issues.issue: The exclusion turns on "pollutants" discharged at or from premises owned, occupied, rented or loaned to any insured, a formulation whose application to ordinary indoor substances in a hospital is a standing point of argument. "Actual, alleged or threatened ... seepage, migration" further widens an already open trigger.

The endorsement replaces the base pollution exclusion in c022, which excluded only discharges that were not "sudden and accidental"; the replacement drops that qualifier entirely. Which formulation applies to a given claim depends on reading the two together.

A hostile fire is defined as one "which becomes uncontrollable or breaks out from where it was intended to be," leaving the friendly/hostile line to be drawn case by case. The definition restates the ambiguity rather than resolving it.

The clause excludes loss, cost or expense arising out of any "request, demand or order" to respond to pollutants, and whether an informal agency letter is a "request" of that kind is not settled by the words. The catch-all "in any way respond to" compounds it.

"Pollutants" is defined as "any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant, including smoke, vapor, soot, fumes, acids, alkalis, chemicals and waste," a general definition trailing a list of industrial specifics. Whether the general words reach substances unlike the listed ones is precisely the general-versus-specific dispute.

The schedule totals the $29,890 premium shown in Item 5, but General Amendatory Endorsement No. 4 (c122) raises the limits "in consideration of the additional premium of $___" with the figure left blank, so the pay plan no longer matches the consideration. The instalment schedule and the endorsement premium cannot both be complete.

General Amendatory Endorsement No. 2 (c098) attaches this form "only as respects Med-Health Financial Services," while the form itself excludes collection-agency errors of "the Insured" without limitation. The two texts state different scopes for the same exclusion.

Coverage is withheld for "any entity which is defined by Wisconsin Statute, Section 655.001 as a health care provider," which imports a statutory classification whose application to particular corporate insureds is contestable. Whether an entity falls within the statutory definition is the operative question.

The Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c089–c090) draws the professional-liability line by a different test — whether the entity is "subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund" — so two endorsements exclude overlapping but differently defined groups. Which test governs a given insured is unresolved.

The statutory definition is "interpreted to include subsidiaries of holding companies of the named insured," a phrase that reverses the ordinary corporate relationship and does not identify whose holding companies are meant. The class of entities swept in cannot be identified with confidence.

Contingent cover depends on an entity that "adheres to the definition of health care provider" being "nevertheless disallowed coverage" by the Fund, and neither "adheres to" nor "disallowed coverage" has a settled meaning. The trigger for the whole contingency turns on those words.

The clause applies the cover over underlying insurance "identified as being listed for contingency coverage purposes," but Item 7 of the declarations (c007) contains no such identification. The condition points to a designation that does not exist in the instrument.

The clause disapplies "Form No. 035(12/87) Professional Services Excluded," but the professional services exclusion actually attached to this policy is Form 035 WI (1/94). The mis-cited form number leaves it uncertain whether the disapplication reaches the form in force.

If the reference is read as ineffective, the Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c089) would continue to bar the very cover the contingent-excess endorsement (c111) purports to grant. The two provisions would then cancel each other out.

General Amendatory Endorsement No. 5 (c124) deletes Form 009-118 (10/92) as "null and void" and substitutes the 2/96 version (c126), yet this endorsement remains in the policy and on the endorsement schedule. It also amends a "Hospital Professional Liability coverage part" that is not attached to this umbrella policy.

The insurer indemnifies "any legal or other expenses necessarily incurred" by the insured in determining which insurer bears the loss, and "necessarily incurred" and "other expenses" are left without any measure. The scope of the reimbursable expense is open.

The definition of ultimate net loss (c024) expressly excludes all loss and legal expenses, and Condition 9 (c051) makes this policy excess over other collectible insurance; this endorsement promises the insured legal expenses of insurer disputes. The provisions treat coverage-dispute costs inconsistently.

Indemnity is payable "only if it is determined that payment of said loss shall be rendered under this policy," which conditions reimbursement of the very expenses of determining coverage on the outcome of that determination. The circularity leaves the promise's practical content unclear.

General Amendatory Endorsement No. 5 (c124) states that Form 009-133 is "deleted from the policy and considered null and void," yet this Trebled Damages Exclusion remains attached and on the endorsement schedule. Whether it forms part of the contract is a question about the fit of the two documents.

The clause first excludes trebled damages and then promises payment of "one-third of the total sum which the insured is obligated to pay," a formula that assumes an exact trebling and does not address mixed awards. The interaction of the exclusion and the one-third payment is not spelled out.
This paragraph is part of Form 009-133, which General Amendatory Endorsement No. 5 (c124) declares deleted and null and void. Its operative force depends entirely on that deletion.

This definition belongs to Form 009-133, which General Amendatory Endorsement No. 5 (c124) deletes from the policy as null and void, while the form remains physically attached. Whether the narrowed meaning of "damages" operates at all turns on that conflict.

The endorsement amends "the policy limits in Item 2," but Item 2 of the declarations is the policy period and the limits appear in Item 3; the consideration is also left blank as "the additional premium of $___." Both defects go to whether and on what terms the limits were changed.

The $20,000,000/$20,000,000 limits stated here contradict the $18,000,000 each occurrence and $9,000,000 aggregate shown in Items 3–5 of the declarations (c005), which are unaltered elsewhere. Which set of limits governs is a direct conflict between the two documents.

The forms said to be "deleted from the policy and considered null and void" — 009-133 (c118–c120) and 009-118 (10/92) (c114) — remain physically attached to the policy and listed on the Schedule of Endorsements. The deletion and the assembled instrument contradict each other.

This replacement endorsement amends "the Policy Territory provisions of the Hospital Professional Liability coverage part attached to the policy," but no such coverage part is attached to this umbrella policy, whose territory clause (c018) applies worldwide. The amendment has no target within the instrument.

The endorsement states an Effective Date of Endorsement of 07/08/1996 but its text says it is "effective on the inception date of the policy unless otherwise stated herein." The two dates in the same document point different ways for the added insured's cover.

Adding Children's Specialty Group, Inc. to Form 009-052 gives it named insured status, which interacts with the Cross Suits Endorsement (c063) and the Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c090) in ways this endorsement does not address. The effective date of that status is also left to c127.

The endorsement's stated Effective Date is 01/01/1997 while its own text makes it "effective on the inception date of the policy unless otherwise stated herein." The internal date conflict matters to when CMG – Brown Deer Campus became insured.

This endorsement adds CMG – Brown Deer Campus "as a Named Insured" in the policy generally, whereas the parallel endorsements (c128, c133) add campuses to Form 009-052; the routes to named insured status are stated inconsistently. Which mechanism governs, and with it the effect of c093's no-automatic-coverage sentence, is unaddressed.

The named insured is amended to "Children's Health System, Inc." whereas the declarations (c001) and every endorsement heading say "Children's Health Systems, Inc." The identity of the first named insured is stated two ways in the same instrument.

Limits are increased for "those individuals and/or entities to whom this coverage applies and that are not subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund," repeating the undefined "subject to the Fund" test and adding an unexplained "to whom this coverage applies." The class of beneficiaries cannot be fixed from the words.

The endorsement is headed to policy HPP-1996-4104-00, the underlying comprehensive general liability policy in Item 7, yet it appears in this umbrella file and speaks of professional liability limits that the Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c089) excludes here. Whether it operates on this policy at all is a genuine question.
